_comment: Raw A/B for #122 (FluidAudio 0.15.4 -> 0.15.5). The same tree was built against each pin in turn and run on osr-harvard-1 (33.6 s, English, multi-chunk) — the corpus that CAN exercise 0.15.5's new seam-duplicate collapse, unlike the jfk/Chinese pairs the first write-up used. Committed because the CHANGELOG's headline measurement was otherwise reproducible only from a temp directory that no longer exists; a number a reader cannot re-derive is the defect this issue is about, one level out.
method: Package.swift pin flipped, swift build, bestasr benchmark --backends fluid-parakeet, pin restored. Which code actually ran was settled on the BINARY, not the checkout: `nm` reports ChunkProcessor.caseVariantCanonicalIds present under the 0.15.5 pin and absent under 0.15.4. The resolved version string does not settle it, and neither does the checked-out source — a stale build artifact survives both.
store_note: The 0.15.4 run also wrote a measurements.jsonl row stamped app_version 0.16.0, which is the version shipping with 0.15.5 — the schema has no FluidAudio field, so the row could not say what condition produced it. That row was removed rather than left to be ranked against honest ones; this file is where the measurement lives instead.
what_it_shows: The transcripts are byte-identical, so the case-gated seam collapse never fired here: a clean reading passage produces no case-differing seam duplicate. The run does exercise upstream 0ac0e414's three word-boundary fallbacks, which are not case-gated and run on any multi-chunk audio. Evidence about the merge path in general; not about the case-gated predicate specifically.
